rail_guard.text: Cairnryan Station: a platform, a bench, a very confident seagull and the whole Scottish rail network.
Hop aboard! The Wildlore rail runs to any station in Great Britain you have visited. Where to?

sailor.text: Belfast, is it? Béal Feirste, as they say over the water. The Selkie is warm, dry and only slightly judgemental about your bag. Aboard you come.

then.text: Raining on the lorry park. The view's still lovely, mind. You just need to wipe it first.
Ferry might be held in this wind. Means I'm parked here with a bacon roll. Worse things happen at sea.
First ferry's loading. Lorries in a long line, seagulls on the roofs. Every morning, same show.

cai_lorry.text: Cairnryan is basically a lorry car park with a lovely view. Hundreds of ferry lorries roll through every day. The seagulls know the timetable better than I do.
In the war this was a big military port, and a railway line ran in just to feed it. The line's long gone, but the road remembers.

then.text: Rain doesn't bother the oysters. They live in the loch. They've never been dry in their lives.
Loch Ryan in fog is lovely and quiet. You hear the ferry horn long before you see the ferry.

cai_oyster.text: The wild oysters in Loch Ryan were here before the ferries and they'll be here after. They're patient. I admire that in a shellfish.
Fàilte, by the way. That means welcome. Say it with a bit of cheek and you'll sound local.

then.text: Wet day? A bacon roll fixes it. It's science, or near enough.
Ferry's delayed in this wind, so I'm doing a roaring trade. Bacon rolls all round, the size of hats.
Grill's on early for the first boat. The seagulls are up even earlier, practising their sad faces.

cai_wife.text: We do a bacon roll the size of a hat. The ferry folk swear by it, and the seagulls swear at it, because they can't get in.
Mòran taing, that's 'many thanks'. I say it forty times a day. It never gets old, and neither does the roll.

then.text: On a sunny day you can see the ferry right across the loch. One day I'll be the one driving it.
It's raining, so I'm practising being a ferry captain. Captains don't mind rain. Seagulls don't either.
Mum says I have to be in when the lights come on. The lights are coming on. See you tomorrow!

cai_kid.text: I'm going to be a ferry captain. Or a seagull. Mum says I'd have to choose by Friday.
Did you know Scotland has nearly eight hundred islands? My nana says some of them are just big rocks with ambition.
